Top review: PROsThese notebooks are excellent, if a little pricey. The cover is professional looking (a smooth matte black) and appropriate for either an office setting or college. The paper is smooth and takes ink well, with minimal bleed through (at least for gel ink). It takes pencil lines without smudging. The ruling lines on the page are a very subtle grey: dark enough to just be visible but light enough to be unobtrusive.The book is "perfect bound," meaning the paper is glued firmly on one side, then the cover applied as a single piece with adhesive at the binding. The entire book is then trimmed to size. This gives the book a nice rectangular shape with straight edges and all 90-degree angles -- no curves. It will sit neatly in a stack with other books. The binding is strong enough and flexible enough to hold together well, even if you aggresively "smush" it flat. The price is a little high for what you get but I find it's still worth it.CONs1. Because the notebook is perfect-bound, it will never sit ENTIRELY flat when open. (A bit of judicious page folding before use will make it lie NEARLY flat -- good enough for me.) If you need a notebook to lie absolutely flat, you will need to get "real" lab notebooks with a stitched binding, which are much more expensive to produce. Those will cost you about 3 times as much as these!2. Also, I wish they made a variant where the width of the graph lines at the top was exactly the same as the width of the ruled lines at the bottom. (This would be non-standard, however. THESE books are standard 5x5 per inch graph at top, and college 5/8 inch ruled at bottom, which is what more people probably want.)
